entries.answer:
1. `SYSTEM_PROMPT = (` opens a parenthesized expression for the concatenated string literals, but the closing `)` never appears before `class ClientInputError`, so the module is syntactically invalid at that point and Python would stop parsing there.[1]

2. `Settings.from_environment` starts `return cls(` and fills several keyword arguments, but after `application_title=os.environ.get(...)` there is no extra closing `)` to terminate the surrounding `cls(...)` call before `def _positive_int`, so that constructor call is left unterminated.[1]

3. In `build_upstream_payload`, `payload: dict[str, Any] = {` starts a dictionary literal that includes `"model"`, `"messages"`, `"temperature"`, `"top_p"`, `"max_tokens"`, `"stream"`, and `"reasoning"`, but the closing `}` is missing before the subsequent `for key in ("frequency_penalty", "presence_penalty"):` loop, making the function syntactically invalid.[1]

4. `_upstream_headers` begins `return {` and adds `"Authorization"`, `"Content-Type"`, `"Accept"`, `"HTTP-Referer"`, and `"X-Title"`, but the dictionary is never closed before `def _api_key`, so the function body contains an unterminated mapping literal.[1]

5. `_api_key` calls `raise UpstreamError(` with `HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and the message `"OPENROUTER_API_KEY is not configured on the server"`, but the closing `)` is missing before `return key.strip()`, leaving the `raise` expression syntactically incomplete.[1]

6. In `_stream_upstream`, the `Request(` call includes `OPENROUTER_URL`, `data=encoded`, `headers=_upstream_headers(_api_key(), settings)`, and `method="POST"`, but the call is not closed before `last_error: Exception | None = None`, so that function also contains an unterminated call expression. [1]

7. The `/v1/models` branch of `do_GET` contains a malformed `_send_json(` payload literal: after `HTTPStatus.OK,` it immediately starts with `"object": "list"` instead of opening a body dictionary with `{`, so the response object is not valid Python syntax.[1]

8. The same `/v1/models` payload is malformed a second time inside `"data": [ ... ]` because the element begins with `"id": MODEL_NAME` instead of opening an item dictionary with `{`, so the list contents are also syntactically invalid.[1]

9. The same `_send_json(` call in the `/v1/models` branch never shows its final closing `)` before the following `return`, so even aside from the malformed literals, the function call itself is left unterminated.[1]

10. In `do_POST`, `tenant_id = _validate_identifier(self.headers, "X-Tenant-ID", TENANT_PATTERN, "default"` is missing its closing `)` before the next assignment begins, so the first identifier-validation call is syntactically incomplete.[1]

11. In `do_POST`, `session_id = _validate_identifier(self.headers, "X-Session-ID", SESSION_PATTERN, uuid.uuid4().hex` is also missing its closing `)` before `body = parse_json_body(self)`, so the second identifier-validation call is likewise syntactically incomplete.[1]

12. In the generic `except Exception:` block of `do_POST`, `_send_json(` is invoked with `HTTPStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` and `{"error": {"message": "Internal server error"}}`, but the closing `)` is missing before `def _handle_json`, so the exception path contains another unterminated call.[1]

13. In `main`, `logging.basicConfig(` includes `level=os.environ.get("LOG_LEVEL", "INFO").upper()` and `format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s"`, but the call is never closed before `settings = Settings.from_environment()`, leaving the function syntactically invalid there as well.[1]

14. `Settings` defines a separate `connect_timeout` field and `from_environment` populates it from `OPENROUTER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, but both `_request_upstream` and `_stream_upstream` call `urlopen(..., timeout=settings.request_timeout)` and never use `settings.connect_timeout`, so one advertised configuration parameter is dead code and misleading.[1]

15. `build_upstream_payload` sets `"stream": bool(body.get("stream", False))`, which is a logic bug because non-boolean truthy inputs such as `"false"` or `[0]` would be coerced to `True` instead of being rejected as invalid request data.[1]

16. `_stream_upstream` suppresses `json.JSONDecodeError` with `continue`, which means malformed upstream SSE payloads are silently discarded instead of raising an error, so clients can receive incomplete output with no indication that chunks were dropped.[1]

17. `_stream_upstream` emits `b"data: [DONE]\n\n"` after the loop over the upstream response even when the upstream side did not send `[DONE]`, so a truncated or prematurely terminated stream can be falsely reported to the client as a cleanly completed stream.[1]

18. `do_POST` catches `UpstreamError` and generic `Exception` at the outer request-handler level and responds with `_send_json(...)`, but the streaming branch calls `_handle_stream(payload)` first, which sends SSE headers immediately; if an error occurs after streaming has started, the handler will try to send a JSON HTTP error body on an already-open event-stream response, producing a corrupted protocol sequence.[1]

that’s all.
